The order of the District Collector dated 14.03.2024, rejecting the application submitted by the petitioner is under challenge in the present writ petition.

2. The petitioner states that he is in absolute possession and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis enjoyment of his family property situate in Survey No.32/6, Kottaikadu Village, Cheyyur Taluk,
Chengalpattu District.
3. The Authorities developed the East Coast Road (ECR) under the Mammallapuram-Puducherry ECR widening project.
They have designed for construction of 'Rain Harvesting Canal'.

4. Mr.J.Muthukumaran, learned Counsel for the petitioner would submit that the Patta land belongs to the petitioner is being utilised for constructing 'Rain Harvesting Canal' and the petitioner submitted a representation to chose an alternate land, which is a Government Poramboke land available.
Since the representation submitted by the petitioner to chose alternate land for construction of 'Rain Harvesting Canal' was rejected, the present writ petition came to be instituted.
5. The order of the District Collector, Chengalpattu is self-speaking.
The order says that during flooding protections are to be provided to the people residing in that locality.

Theerefore,
construction of 'Rain Harvesting Canal' is of paramount importance.
The project has been designed by https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis National Highways Authority & Research Station and various aspects were considered for implementing the projects.

sentences.text: 6. Scheme is research oriented to sub-serve the public good.

If at all Patta land belongs to the petitioner is to be taken for implementing the public project, no doubt the petitioner would be entitled for compensation and such compensation is to be settled in accordance with the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act.
However, Court cannot interfere with such welfare projects being implemented to protect the people from flooding during rainy seasons.
'Rain Harvesting Canal' is an important project, which is to be implemented by the Government as per the project scheme approved by the National Highways Authority of India.

Therefore, alternation of the Scheme or deviation of the route is exclusively under the domain of the research/expert body in the field and the High Court cannot substitute any opinion for implementation of such research oriented schemes.
7. The representation submitted by the petitioner to chose an https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis alternate route was considered and rejected.
That being the factum, this Court is not inclined to entertain the writ petition.
Accordingly, this Writ Petition stands dismissed at the admission stage itself.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
